On 2023-05-20, the user supplied a passage explaining that median life expectancy is the age by which half of a population has died, not the age most people die. It contrasted late Stone Age life expectancy of about 33 years with about 80 years in wealthy nations today and a global average of about 67 years. In the Stone Age, early childhood (birth to age five) was especially dangerous; someone who survived to the median age had a good chance of living into their fifties, sixties, or seventies. Modern life expectancy is higher mainly because almost everyone now survives to adulthood; among adults who reached adulthood, lifespan improvements are more modest. The passage’s author says they prefer a world where children are safe to one offering 20 or 30 extra years of old age.

On 2023-05-20, the assistant answered passage questions 25–30 as follows: 25 D, 26 A, 27 A, 28 A, 29 A, 30 B. Question 27’s answer A (“It is now possible to accurately predict how long an individual will live”) is not supported by the passage; option D, about lower life expectancy in less wealthy countries, is more consistent with the figures given.
